biggestGap: The flesh is driven past the red channel's ceiling — R is pinned at 255 across 48.3% of the watermelon cut face and 31.2% of the citrus half (plate-01 flesh clips 0.6%, plate-02's lemon half clips 0.00%), so the pulp reads as flat self-lit candy with all internal anatomy carried only by G/B, and the seeds cannot go black.
evidence: MEASURED, 640x360 native. (1) Round 1's named gap is genuinely fixed. Vertical scan through the r2-05 watermelon cut face at x=337: rind y198-204 lum 40.3/41.9/44.1/46.3/46.8 -> pith y206-209 lum 135.5/175.2/167.9/247.8 -> flesh y211-245 lum 76-135. The pale band is 5.3x the rind value and 2.1x the flesh median. r1-05 at x=340 had NO pale band anywhere: y198-254 runs 0/7/11/18/25/28/45/54/34/30/27, i.e. flesh lum 25-56 with the pith absent. Citrus, r2-08 horizontal scan y=246: pith lum 236.6 at x=238 and 236.1/237.4 at x=282-284 vs flesh 149.8-162.3 (1.5x). Seeds, membranes, radial fibre and a rind/pith/flesh edge stack are all now readable at 6x zoom. That axis moved. (2) Cut-face wetness is also in-band now: at matched pixel scale (face resampled to ~65px) the fraction of pixels >15 lum above a 2px blur is render-wm 21.76% (mean|highpass| 22.83) vs plate-01 27.43% (23.24) and plate-02 13.76% (10.71); render-citrus 18.02% (11.73). Foam density is no longer the problem. (3) What is now the problem is exposure of the material itself. Watermelon cut face (n=2613 px): mean RGB (233.7, 95.9, 90.1), R>=255 on 48.3% of pixels; citrus near half incl. peel (n=4509): mean (173.0, 105.1, 46.0), R>=255 on 31.2%. References: plate-01 flesh box (560-800, 380-520) mean (188.4, 72.2, 55.8) with R>=255 on 0.6%; plate-02 near lemon half mean (141.8, 98.5, 45.6) with R>=250 on 0.00%. Direct consequence for anatomy: the darkest 5% of our watermelon face (the seeds) is RGB (130.5, 21.9, 10.7), lum 53.4, only 2.14x below the flesh median of 114.3 -- they read as dark red bruises. Plate-01's darkest 5% is RGB (23.2, 5.2, 2.8), lum 15.4, 5.48x below its median of 84.4: real seeds are near-black occluders. Second consequence: the pith ring peaks at lum 247.3 +/- 5.5 sampled at 48 angles around the face (CV 2.2%) -- identical brightness top, bottom, lit side and shadow side, which is a painted constant-value stroke, not a lit tissue band; its width also swings from 0.0 to 11.2 px (CV 0.476), so it vanishes entirely on some spokes. Blind test: handed these unlabelled I pick the render instantly off the candy-pink clipped disc and the uniform cream ring alone, before resolution enters into it.
fix: In /home/claude/juice/src/fruit/species.js, buy back red-channel headroom in fleshMaterial. Two coupled changes: (a) drop the pulp albedos about a stop -- watermelon fleshHex '#e33455' is linear R 0.73 and orange fleshHex '#ff9d1e' is linear R 1.0; real cut pulp is linear R 0.35-0.45, so target '#c02742' and '#e07d14' -- and (b) stop the SSS emissiveNode from stacking additively on top of the key. Right now it returns sssColor * sss(0.6) * sssMask * (wrap^2*0.50 + fres*0.30) with sssColor = juiceColor ('#ff2f52', linear R 1.0), so the lit half of the face gets albedo AND up to ~0.3 linear extra red from the same direction. Gate it by the inverse of the key term instead -- multiply by (1 - wrap) or by saturate(1 - directLuma) -- so transmission only appears where the surface is turning away, which is where real translucency shows. Verify with the same probe: R>=255 on the watermelon cut-face ellipse must fall under 5%, and the darkest 5% of that face must reach lum <= 25 so the seeds actually read black.
notes: Score is up from 21 because the anatomy separation the piece was told to fix is measurably fixed and the foam statistics now land between the two plates. It stays under 60 because the piece is still instantly identifiable as a game render on colour alone.
